TO BE ANSWERED ON 27.12.2018 
 
PREFERENCE TO HANDLOOM CLOTHES 
 
2743. SHRI PRAHLAD SINGH PATEL 
 
 Will the Minister of TEXTILES वस्त्र मंरी 
  
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether handloom clothes are given preference in the purchase of clothes as per the 
requirement of various Central Ministries;  
(b)  if so, the detailed procedure for purchasing of such clothes; 
(c) the quantity and amount of mill -made cloth as well as handloom c loth purchased by the 
Ministry of Railways out of the total purchase of cloth es during the year 2017 -2018; 
and 
(d)  whether the Ministry of Railways is likely to be directed that under the policy only 
handloom clothes should be purchased to provide employment to the weavers? 
उत्तर 
ANSWER 
वस्त्र राज्य मंरी (श्री अजय टम्टा) 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR TEXTILES 
(SHRI AJAY TAMTA) 
 
(a) to (d): Association of Corporations &  Apex Societies of Handlooms (ACASH) is the 
nodal office of Ministry of Textiles, Government of India to supply handloom clothes to the 
Central Ministries and their Departments.  ACASH is supplying handloom cloths through its

handloom cloth es worth Rs. 97.00 crores . Ministry of Railways is procuring the required 
handloom clothes through GeM.  However, from time to time, directions have been issued by 
the Government of India to various Ministries/Departments to purchase handloom clothes from 
ACASH.

LOK SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.2745 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 27.12.2018 
 
CREATION OF JOBS 
 
2745.   SHRIMATI VASANTHI M:  
 
Will the Minister of TEXTILES वस्त्र मंरी 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether there is a need to create more jobs in textile, garments and leather industry to 
generate employment for the unskilled youth in the country; 
 
(b) whether it is also true that the Government is working on this direction to create jobs in these 
segments; and 
 
(c)        if so, the details thereof? 
उत्तर 
ANSWER 
वस्त्र राज्य मंरी (श्री अजय टम्टा) 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR TEXTILES 
(SHRI AJAY TAMTA) 
 
(a) to (c):  Yes Madam. As per Economic Survey 2016 -17, Textiles, Apparels and Leather 
Goods segments have potential of generating more jobs among industrial sector.  Government 
introduced special package of reforms for generation of around 1.11 crore jobs in apparel and 
made-ups sector. The package includes a  slew of measures which are labour friendly and 
would promote  employment generation, economies of scale and boost exports . Moreover, 
Government is providing additional production linked incentive of 10% under the Amended 
Technology Upgradation Fund Scheme (ATUFS) for promoting employment in garmenting 
segment. Furthermore, the Government has designed Pradhan Mantri  Paridhan Rojgar 
Protsahan Yojana (PMPRPY) to incentivize employers in the apparel sector for generation of 
new employment. The special package has been extended to made -ups sector to provide 
additional impetus to employment generation. Apart from the above, the Government has been 
implementing skill development programme  (SAMARTH) for enhancing employment 
potential of textile workers, the North Eastern Region Textile Promotion Scheme (NERPS), 
Comprehensive scheme for Development of Powerloom Sector, Scheme  for Integrated Textile 
Parks (SITPs), schemes for development of silk, wool,  jute, handloom, and handicrafts sectors 
with the aim of enhancing production and employment generation in these segments. Further, 
the Government has approved special package of Rs.2600 crore for the years 2017-18 to 2019-
20 to generate employment in leather and footwear sector.  So far, around 1.2 lakh unemployed 
persons have been given skill training in the leather and footwear sector and out of them, 
96,444 persons have been given placement in the sector.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT & HIGHWAYS 
LOK SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2747 
ANSWERED  ON  27th DECEMBER, 2018 
NEW  ROAD MAP  FOR ACCIDENT PREVENTION 
†2747. SHRI  KUNWAR PUSHPENDRA SINGH CHANDEL:  
Will the Minister of ROADTRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS  
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री 
be pleased to state:  
(a) whether the Government has taken note of the accidents happening on various 
National Highways;  
(b) if so, whe ther the Government has developed any technique based new roadmap 
to prevent them;  
(c) if so, the details thereof; 
(d) whether the Government has constituted a study team for improving the 
infrastructure of National Highways;  
(e) if so, the details thereof; and  
(f) whether the Government is planning to determine rankings of National 
Highways? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE 
MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
(SHRI  MANSUKH  L. MANDAVIYA) 
 
(a) to ( c)  : Yes Madam, the Ministry collects data/information in the prescribed format 
from the Police Department of all States/UTs. They provide data/information to this Ministry 
in the prescribed format on road accidents on all roads including National Highways from 
time to time.   
 
The Government has launched a mobile app for highway users i.e. “SukhadYatra 
1033” which enables highways users to report potholes and other safety hazards on National 
Highways including accidents. 
Ministry has taken following steps to prevent accidents on National Highways 
(i)           Rectification of identified Black spots, 
(ii)         Road Safety Audits are being carried out at all stages of development of the 
highway i.e. design / construction / operation stages. 
(iii)       Facilities such as Foot Over bridges & underpasses are being provided wherever 
required, for safe crossing of pedestrians and other road users. 
(iv)       Capacity building through training of NHAI field staff /Concessionaires / 
Contractors / Consultants engaged in NHAI project works throughout India. 
(v)         Road Safety Week is observed every calendar year for spreading awareness 
about safer behaviour of road users on National Highways. 

 
 
Apart from the above, highway advisory service Phase II was launched in 12 NH 
stretches with capsules consisting of static content related to road safety awareness, 
adherence to road safety rules and live content related to situation of traffic on route. This 
program was started on 23.04.2018 and concluded on 21.11.2018 and was broadcasted 
through All India Radio. 
 
(d) to  ( f)  :  The Government has already approved a National Road Safety Policy in March 
2010.  This Policy is based on the four E’s of Road Safety viz. (i) Education (ii) Emergency (iii) 
Enforcement (iv) Engineering (roads as well as vehicles) and outlines various policy measures 
such as promoting awareness, establishing road safety information data base, encouraging 
safer road infrastructure including application of intelligent transport, enforcement of safety 
laws etc.

ANSWERED ON 27TH DECEMBER, 2018 
 
 
NHS IN KERALA 
 
2748. PROF. K.V. THOMAS:  
DR. P.K. BIJU:  
 
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the number of National Highways in the country, especially in Kerala that have been 
expanded into four lanes and six lanes, if so, the details thereof;  
 
(b)  whether there are objections for the development of the National Highways into four lanes 
and six lanes and the steps taken to settle these objections; 
  
(c)  the total allotment and utilization of money to the National Highways in Kerala during the last 
five years;  
 
(d)  the length of NHs during the last ten years in the country and the length of NHs built in 
Kerala during the same period;  
 
(e)  the number of such highway projects in the State that have been funded fully by the Centre 
and through PPP mode during the above period; and  
 
(f)  the details of major NH stretches currently under construction in the State including PPP and 
toll projects? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE  
MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT & HIGHWAYS 
 
(SHRI MANSUKHL. MANDVIYA) 
 
(a) Development of various National Highways including their expansion to four/six lane is 
carried out subject to traffic, availability of funds and inter -se priority of works. During 
the current financial year 2018-19, 1719Km of various National Highways in the country 
including Kerala have been expanded to Four/six/eight lane out of which 4 Km length 
falls in Kerala. 
 
(b) Objections received from the land owners for development of National Highways into 
four/six/eight lanes are examined by the respective Competent Authority for Land 
Acquisition (CALA) and are disposed of based on the merit as per National Highways 
Act 1956. 
 
(c) During the last five years, a sum of Rs 3500 Crore for development and maintenance of 
various National Highways were allotted out of which Rs 3293 Crore has been utilized. 

 
(d)  During the last ten years, 57839 Km of National Highways in the country including 
Kerala were built/constructed/ developed out of which 230 Km length falls in Kerala. 
 
(e) All Natio nal Highways projects in Kerala  have been fully funded by the Central 
government except three projects of National Highways Authority of India  (NHAI) 
which have been funded through PPP mode  and two projects which are funded to the 
extent of 50% by the Government of Kerala. 
 
(f) At present, nine major National Highway projects each costing more than Rs 300 Crore 
are under construction including PPP/Toll projects.

ACCIDENTS DUE TO BROKEN ROADS AND STRAY ANIMALS 
 
2749. SHRI NAGENDRA PRATAP SINGH PATEL: 
  
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS  
 
सड़क परिवहन औि िाजमार्ग मंत्री 
be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether as per the news item published in ‘Navbharat Times’  dated 4.12.2018, 2600 
persons have lost their lives due to broken roads and stray animals in Uttar Pradesh; 
 
(b)  if so, the steps being taken by the Government to check roaming of stray animals on the 
roads; 
 
(c)  the steps being taken by the Government to check the accidents of two wheeler vehicles 
taking place very often due to excreta of increasing number of stray animals on roads; 
 
(d)  the details of assistance being provided b y the Government to the injured and the 
dependents of those who died in accidents; and 
 
(e)  whether the Government provides financial assistance and employment to them, if so, 
the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
    THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT & HIGHWAYS 
 
(SHRI MANSUKH L. MANDAVIYA) 
 
(a) to ( c) Ministry is primarily responsible for the development and m aintenance of 
National Highways  in the country . As per ‘ Road A ccidents in India 201 7’ 
Publication by Transport Research Wing  of Ministry of Road Transport and  
Highways, 2608 persons were killed on road network in the S tate of Uttar Pradesh in 
the year 2017 , due to collision with animal s, accident due to pot holes and ongoing 
road works/under construction works.  To address road safety concern s, Ministry has 
issued guidelines to carry out Road safety Audit for all the new road projects having 
length of 5 km or more at  the stage of Detailed Project Report (DPR)  / Engineering 
Design. Adequate mitigation measures including construction of Foot Over Bridges 

(FOBs), underpasses /overpasses /cattle underpasses, Road signages, Road Marking, 
delineators, c rash barrier etc .  are made as an integral part of the highways 
development projects depending upon the site requirement, land availability etc.  
 
(d) & (e) In cases of hit and run acci dent where the identity of  motor vehicle can not be 
ascertained a compensation of Twenty five thousand  rupees  in respect of death and 
Twelve thousand and five hundred rupees in cases of grievous hurt is provided from 
the Solatium Fund under section 161 of the Motor vehicle Act 1988.
